name: The Plane Tree of the Botterbrug

location.address: Next to the former girls' orphanage, Oude Delft 116 at the Botterbrug, Delft

access: Free. Municipal garden at the Oude Delft canal and Botterbrug, listed visitable and visible in the register.
transport: About 0.5 km north of Delft station; a few minutes' walk from the Markt via Oude Delft.
story:
Nothing else on this stretch of the Oude Delft comes close: seen from above, the plane tree at the Botterbrug is one broad round crown spreading over the canal edge, the largest along the water here. It stands in a small municipal garden beside the former girls' orphanage at Oude Delft 116, and the national register of monumental trees lists it as open to visit and visible from the street.

That register is also where its age comes from. It puts the planting somewhere between 1880 and 1890, which makes the tree about 140 years old, give or take a decade. It records nothing else: no story behind the planting, no name of whoever chose the spot, and no measurement of the trunk.

What the tree has lived through is easier to say. It was already well grown when Delft was occupied in 1940, and it has watched well over a century of boats on the canal and walkers crossing the bridge. Like every London plane it sheds its bark in plates, so the trunk is a patchwork of grey, olive and cream.

The register counts it as a single tree standing on its own rather than one of a row. Nobody has published its girth or its height. If you have put a tape measure round it, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its crown, the single largest along this stretch of the Oude Delft. It stands at the Botterbrug bridge, beside the former girls' orphanage at Oude Delft 116.

name: The Plane Tree at the Annageer corner

location.address: Nieuwe Plantage at the corner with Annageer, Delft

access: Free. Public park strip on the old rampart (Nieuwe Plantage), listed visitable in the register.
transport: About 1.2 km north-west of Delft station; the Plantage ring is a 15 minute walk from the Markt.
story:
The whole recorded history of this plane tree is one line in the national register: it was planted during the renovation of Delft's city ramparts. The line gives no year. What the register does give is a planting band of 1880 to 1890, which puts the tree at roughly 130 to 145 years old, and that band is the only date anybody has published for it.

It stands where the Nieuwe Plantage meets the Annageer, on the strip of park that now runs along the old rampart line. From above it is one large rounded crown at the junction of the paths, touching its neighbours but plainly its own tree. The register files it under the municipality, in a park setting, open to visit.

In its time on the old wall the tree has stood through the occupation of 1940 to 1945 and well over a century of Delft walking past on its way somewhere else. Like every London plane it sheds its bark in plates, leaving the trunk a patchwork of grey, olive and cream.

It is also the start of a short walk. The elms of Kalverbos stand about 90 metres away, with that park's three planes close beside them. Nobody has published this tree's girth or height; if you have measured it, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the large rounded crown right at the path junction where the Nieuwe Plantage meets the Annageer. It stands about 90 metres from the Kalverbos elms; its crown touches its neighbours'.
